title: Accepted into UD's Graduate CIS Program
body: After completing my undergraduate degree, I was accepted into the University of Delaware's Computer and Information Sciences graduate program. I will continue developing my software engineering skills while exploring more advanced areas of computer science.

title: Adopted NestJS for Personal Projects
body: After learning NestJS in a full-stack software engineering course, I quickly became a fan of its structured, opinionated approach to backend development. I began using it in my personal projects, marking my transition away from Express.js.

title: Graduated from the University of Delaware
body: Graduated as a first generation college student with a B.S. in Computer Science, building a strong foundation in software engineering and full-stack development.

title: Attended HenHacks For the Second Time
body: Participated in the University of Delaware's HenHacks hackathon for the second time, building a full-stack application with a team and further strengthening my skills in rapid development, collaboration, and problem-solving under pressure.

title: Deployed My First Full-Stack Monorepo Application
body: Deployed my first full-stack application using a monorepo architecture, gaining experience managing a shared codebase across multiple parts of an application.

title: Started Learning NestJS
body: Built a full-stack group expense-splitting application using NestJS, Prisma, and Auth0 for Google authentication. Learned how to structure a backend using NestJS's opinionated architecture and object-oriented programming principles.

title: Began My Senior Capstone and Internship Search
body: Started my senior capstone project while applying for internships focused on full-stack web development, with the goal of gaining practical industry experience.

title: Shifted Toward Independent Development
body: Transitioned toward more independent development, using personal projects and career preparation to strengthen my ability to learn independently, solve problems without formal coursework, and build consistently on my own.

title: Deployed My First MERN Application
body: Built and deployed an anonymous note-posting website using the MERN stack and Vercel, marking my first experience taking a full-stack application from development to production.

title: Switched to Tailwind CSS
body: Moved from vanilla CSS to Tailwind CSS, learning how modern styling tools can accelerate development, improve consistency, and make interfaces easier to maintain.

title: Attended My First Hackathon: HenHacks
body: Participated in the University of Delaware's HenHacks hackathon. Although my team did not win, the experience taught me how to brainstorm and build under pressure while strengthening my understanding of GitHub, branching, version control, and collaborative development.

title: Adopted TypeScript
body: Transitioned my projects from JavaScript to TypeScript, gaining a stronger appreciation for type safety, maintainability, and scalability in modern web applications.

title: Started Working in UD's CS Department
body: Became a teaching assistant for the University of Delaware's computer science department and joined the Lerner College of Business and Economics Tech Deck as a technical support assistant. These roles strengthened my communication, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.

title: Started Learning React
body: Began exploring component-based development with React. Concepts like state, props, and hooks were initially challenging, but once they clicked, I gained a much deeper understanding of how modern frontend applications are structured and scaled.

title: Started Studying Computer Science at UD
body: Started my Computer Science degree at the University of Delaware, gaining my first formal exposure to computer science theory, algorithms, and low-level programming. The coursework challenged me while giving me a stronger technical foundation.

title: Deepened My MongoDB Knowledge
body: Dived deeper into MongoDB, learning data modeling, schema design with Mongoose, CRUD operations, and how to integrate a database into a MERN stack application.

title: Explored Full-Stack Development
body: Started combining MongoDB, Express, React, and Node.js to build small applications. This marked the beginning of my journey into full-stack web development.

title: Took My First Steps into Backend Development
body: Dove into Node.js and Express and began building APIs, realizing how backend services connect frontend applications to real-world data. This expanded my development experience beyond frontend-focused projects.

title: Accelerated My Learning During the Pandemic
body: Used the pandemic as an opportunity to strengthen my JavaScript skills and rebuild my club website from scratch, learning the value of iteration, experimentation, and continuous improvement.

title: Built My First Major Project
body: Built a website for my high school club using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Firebase. This was my first experience connecting a frontend application to a backend database.

title: Started Learning Web Development
body: Began experimenting with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript through YouTube tutorials and simple static websites, taking my first steps into web development.
